question_issues.evidence: The sha256-verified supplied input data/seqs/LuxC.faa (sha256 7ce47aaed2c5, byte-identical packaged copy read directly) contains 12 records, five of which are UniProtKB/TrEMBL entries, not Swiss-Prot: tr|A0A644X819|A0A644X819_9ZZZZ (OS=bioreactor metagenome), tr|A0A2H5XB72|A0A2H5XB72_9BACT (OS=bacterium HR17), tr|Q5DZ03|Q5DZ03_ALIF1, tr|B6ESM7|B6ESM7_ALISL, tr|S3DGB3|S3DGB3_9GAMM. The reference LuxC.domtbl (sha256 fc3da85a) rows 4, 9, 12, 14 and 15 report exactly these TrEMBL targets. Neither 'Swiss-Prot' nor 'from bioluminescent bacteria' (a bioreactor-metagenome and an uncultured-bacterium isolate are in the set) describes the actual population. This is a false input-population claim in the base question; it needs a prose correction (e.g. 'UniProtKB records (Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL) of LuxC-family enzymes') via the existing description-correction route, with no science, tolerance or check changes.
question_issues.quote: Unaligned protein sequences in FASTA format (UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot records of LuxC-family enzymes from bioluminescent bacteria) — the target search database.

question_issues.evidence: hmmsearch --domtblout and pyhmmer TopHits.write(format=domains) emit fixed-width space-aligned columns, not tab-separated fields. The hash-verified reference LuxC.domtbl (sha256 fc3da85a) uses space-run separators: 'tr|B6ESM7|B6ESM7_ALISL         -            476 LuxC ...' (line 4, read directly). The grading addendum and grader treat rows as whitespace-delimited (split(None, 22)), and the valid-alternative probe domtbl-separator-representation (rows rewritten to tabs) passes only because the comparison is whitespace-based, confirming the canonical format is not tab-separated. The base question claim contradicts the addendum's whitespace rule; it should be corrected to whitespace-delimited/space-aligned wording without altering the field list or any check.

rationale: The candidate grader, controls, probes and environment isolation are sound: 17/17 fresh controls met expected outcomes (reference, empty, misplaced, recomputed, alternative, two missing-file and ten probe records with executed mutations and post-probe submission hashes); the wrong-answer probes for LuxC.hmm (NSEQ/CKSUM/MSV keystat change, single-digit emission change) and LuxC.domtbl (E-value outside band, score/coordinate/accuracy change, description truncation, row deletion, row reordering) are meaningful scientific negatives, and the two valid-alternative probes (DATE/COM provenance-only edit, whitespace-to-tab representation) correctly pass. The LuxC.hmm answer fixture was excluded with a validated removal receipt (excluded_files_absent=true) and a fresh passing reference execution, and no LuxC search-result fixture exists in the packaged tables (verified by listing distribution members: only PF02826, RREFam, bmyD and A0A089QRB9 tables). However, the base public question contains two false prose claims that remain defects even though all numerical controls pass: (1) the FASTA search database is described as 'UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot records of LuxC-family enzymes from bioluminescent bacteria', but the sha256-verified input contains 12 records of which five are UniProtKB/TrEMBL (tr|) entries, including a bioreactor-metagenome and an uncultured-bacterium isolate (reference domtbl rows 4, 9, 12, 14, 15 report these TrEMBL targets); (2) the domtbl field order is described as 'tab-separated', but canonical --domtblout output (and the reference file) is fixed-width space-aligned, and the grading addendum/grader treat fields as whitespace-delimited. Both are correctable through the existing prose-correction route without changing the scientific target, reference outputs, tolerances or checks, so the proper disposition is revise rather than blocked; after correction, the affected review must be repeated on the new candidate.

The packaged tests/data/tables directory contains only PF02826, RREFam, bmyD and A0A089QRB9 tables (verified by listing the distribution members), so no LuxC domtbl/hit-statistics fixture is bundled anywhere.

Remaining LuxC-named packaged files are byte-identical copies of the supplied inputs (msa/LuxC.sto sha256 e2cf20e9 and seqs/LuxC.faa sha256 7ce47aae, both verified by direct read and equal to the trusted-input identities) or different-input fixtures (LuxC.weighted.sto, LuxC.sto.ssi, the distinct 5993-byte msa/LuxC.faa) or a score-free hmmalign alignment (LuxC.hmmalign.sto); none contains the requested per-hit scores, E-values, accuracies, ranking or model parameters.

Grader answer-embedding: the grader reads both endpoint values dynamically from --reference-dir and grounds NAME/ACC and target identities/lengths/descriptions against the BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR copy; no answers, dimensions or hashes are embedded (full grader code reviewed).

Coverage scope: the dependency-assets summary inspected all 372 installed regular files across psutil and pyhmmer; my own package-source search for LuxC matched only the enumerated tests/data fixtures and test-source references. Residual coverage is per the stated catalog scope (not an exhaustive semantic audit of every byte of every file), but the answer-bearing asset classes (prebuilt LuxC model, LuxC hit tables) were enumerated, searched and, where an identity copy existed, verified removed; the supplied asset-value hints found no floating-literal endpoint matches (findings list empty, all candidates unsupported non-Python fixtures).
answer_isolation.rationale: The solver-visible evidence consists of the two intended input files (whose identical copies legitimately remain in the installed distribution) plus the cleaned pyhmmer 0.12.3 installation with the one answer-bearing fixture excluded and the removal validated by fresh passing reference execution. No LuxC.hmm answer copy or LuxC domtbl/hit-statistics fixture is visible to the solver, and the grader compares dynamically against the reference with input grounding through the trusted-input directory. The value literals in probe scripts are test-only assertions on reference files, not solver-visible assets.

evidence: Executed control records (candidate sha256 f8d0ef3b): reference submission passed; recomputed run (LuxC.hmm 4006260) passed hmm_model_content; independent alternative run (LuxC.hmm cbc5ecba, Pipeline fed from the saved-file round-trip) passed; all three outputs canonicalize to the same model body, establishing valid-answer acceptance across construction paths.

Wrong-answer rejection is demonstrated by executed mutations, not parser failures: hmm-keystat-change (NSEQ 13 to 12, CKSUM changed, MSV intercept perturbed; post-probe hash 3c0669cc, hmm_model_content False with message 'model body differs ... line 11' while hmm_ascii_format stayed True) and hmm-emission-parameter-change (single digit 2.07294 to 2.17294, token count preserved at 26; post-probe hash 2a194595, hmm_model_content False at 'line 25', structure intact). Both reach the decoded-model comparison rather than a crash.

Structural guard: hmm-double-model (post-probe hash 8ea90c22) fails hmm_ascii_format ('file contains more than one HMM model') while the first model still matches content, isolating the one-model rule; empty/misplaced submissions fail on missing files rather than passing.

Provenance normalization is scientifically justified: the repeatability records show the model body identical across controlled reruns with only HMMER version/DATE/COM provenance lines differing, and the valid-alternative probe hmm-provenance-date-com (post-probe hash e7047ef2) passes all checks. The grader compares the canonical re-serialization of the decoded model (DATE/COM excluded), so a different decimal rendering of an identical decoded value would pass while any decoded-value change fails, consistent with the public wording.

Input-derived identity is checked against the immutable trusted copy, not a solver-controllable file: check_hmm_content reads data/msa/LuxC.sto via BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR and enforces NAME equal to '#=GF ID LuxC' and ACC equal to '#=GF AC PF05893.5' (the independent alternative run, whose HMM was built from the staged inputs, passes; the packaged alignment header lines 2-3 confirm these values, and lines 7-9 carry the GA/TC/NC cutoffs the model must copy).

Scientific equivalence holds by construction of the task target: the question requests reproduction of the reference-default hmmbuild computation, so exact decoded-parameter equality of the Plan7 build is the defined contract. Valid-answer acceptance is supported by three independently produced outputs (controller reference, construction rerun, independent search-from-saved-file run) all canonicalizing identically; no wider-precision or cross-stack portability claim is made beyond these recorded executions.
comparisons.rationale: The decoded Plan7 model comparison is applied through the installed native HMMER3 reader: the submission is parsed, canonically re-serialized (DATE/COM provenance lines excluded) and compared to the reference canonical form as exact string equality, complemented by a structural line/token-count guard against extra content and a second-model check. This represents the full model: NAME/ACC/DESC, length, architecture flags, NSEQ/EFFN/CKSUM, GA/TC/NC cutoff lines copied from the alignment, STATS LOCAL calibration and every per-position emission/transition parameter at stored precision. The format's own stored precision limits how thin a wrong answer can be while remaining well-formed; the author's note that the wider-precision acceptance clause is effectively untestable in this ASCII format is accurate, so the acceptance is not permissive in practice.

evidence: Executed control records: reference (fc3da85a) and recomputed runs pass; the independent alternative run (domtbl 89a96c75, hash-differing from the reference because the search reads the saved ASCII HMM through a fresh Pipeline) passes all checks in full, establishing valid-answer acceptance for a different execution path.

The E-value relative tolerance (10% of the reference value, zero equals zero exactly) is corroborated by recorded executions: the reference domtbl is byte-identical across both controlled replays, while the independent run differs from the reference only in one E-value cell (about 4% relative, one-significant-digit exponent rounding: 2.3e-169 vs 2.4e-169) with every other compared column byte-identical. Because bit scores, coordinates, identity columns, domain index and accuracy must match exactly, the tolerance cannot admit a wrong scoring method; it only absorbs last-digit rounding of E-value formatting, matching the addendum's stated basis. The exact 10% boundary is declared publicly and remains a stated limitation, not hidden permissiveness.

Wrong-answer rejection is demonstrated by executed, well-formed mutations: domtbl-evalue-tolerance (E-values far outside band, row count and other columns preserved, domtbl_hit_rows False), domtbl-score-coord-change (bit scores, hmm-from coordinate, accuracy changed, E-values untouched, False at 'rank 1: column 16 is 3, reference has 2'), domtbl-desc-truncate (description truncation with all 22 columns intact, False), domtbl-row-missing (11 vs 12 rows, False) and domtbl-row-reorder (rows swapped, count unchanged, False on the positional identity check). All mutating probes record probe_valid_execution true with post-probe submission hashes.

Rank order and cross-file identity: rows are matched positionally in the tool's canonical order (verified decreasing full-sequence score 553.3, 551.0, 546.9 and so on in the reference file read directly), and target identity, accessions, tlen and descriptions are additionally grounded against the trusted FASTA via BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR (passing control messages include 'database-grounded target identities', evidencing that the grounding branch executed), so a row describing a target absent from the supplied database fails even if it copies reference structure.

Dependency across outputs: the domtbl must carry the query name/accession and qlen of the model built in Task A; the independent run searched from the saved LuxC.hmm round-trip and reproduced the reference exactly, and the exact string columns (query name LuxC, accession PF05893.5, qlen 400) couple the two files consistently with the recorded reference values.

Structural format guard (domtbl_table_format) compares the canonical hmmsearch preamble exactly against the reference's three fixed comment lines (read directly; they contain no program-version text, so the author's preamble-strictness concern is immaterial for this instance) and rejects comment-after-row rows, short rows, blank rows and nonfinite/negative E-values; the whitespace-to-tab representation probe passes, matching the stated whitespace-delimited contract (while exposing the base question's incorrect 'tab-separated' wording, reported separately).
comparisons.rationale: The domain hit table is compared row-by-row in canonical rank order with exact equality on identity/accession columns, tlen, qlen, domain index/count, all six coordinates, both bit scores, both bias values and the per-domain posterior accuracy, and a 10% relative tolerance on the three E-value columns only. Target identities, lengths, descriptions and tlen are grounded against the immutable trusted copy of the supplied FASTA, so the row population cannot be invented from reference values alone. Scientifically consequential wrong outputs fail through executed well-formed mutations, not crashes or malformed files.

source_coverage.rationale: The converted notebook has exactly two terminal scientific results: the Plan7 profile HMM built from the seed alignment (builder.build_msa with default Builder/Background; serialized by hmm.write) and the hmmsearch-default domain hit table (pipeline.search_hmm; serialized by hits.write(format=domains)). Both are requested outputs with their own structural and scientific checks. The coverage ledger accounts for all 13 recorded literal source operations: the result operations map to the two graded endpoints, the input-file opens map to the two supplied inputs, and the remaining calls are configuration/serialization support. The two excluded items in plan.json are legitimately non-endpoints: hmm.consensus is a property inspection wholly contained in the exported HMM file, and print(ali) is the default text presentation of a single top-hit domain alignment whose coordinates and scores are fully contained in LuxC.domtbl; neither is an independent terminal result, and no additional scientific branch (any other model, table, plot or statistic) exists in the original source. The question's Task A framing additionally preserves the HMM as a scientific deliverable rather than a mere intermediate, consistent with the plan.json source evidence.
remaining_validation: The structural check domtbl_table_format has no executed content-level negative probe (wrong preamble, short row or nonfinite/negative E-value); only missing-file and sibling-probe indirect failures cover it. It is a declared structural check, so this does not block the science audit, but a wrong-preamble/short-row probe should be run on any revised candidate to complete the suite.

The E-value 10% boundary itself was never probed at exactly 10% relative deviation; the grader's strict inequality means a value exactly at the boundary passes, consistent with the public wording (values outside the band are wrong answers), but no boundary case is on record.
